points.description: States that the best case occurs when the input array is already sorted (in the desired order). Do not accept reverse-sorted/descending (that is the worst case).

levels.says: Vaguely says the array is 'nearly sorted' or 'in order' without clearly stating already sorted.

points.description: States that the number of operations is N (linear, O(N)), where N is the length of the array/number of elements. Equivalent: n comparisons, n-1 comparisons, or linear time. Do not accept N^2 / O(n^2).

levels.says: Says linear/O(n) or proportional to n without naming N, or gives N-1 without linking to array length.

rubric.notes: Full marks: already sorted array and N (linear, O(N)) operations. Half-ish credit for vague versions of either. No marks for reverse-sorted or N^2 answers.
